objective: Download and install dependencies for a Backstage project with NPM/Yarn: Yarn workspaces, the lockfile, backstage-cli versions:bump and keeping @backstage packages aligned
secondaryObjectives: Compile a Backstage project with TypeScript: yarn tsc, type checking across packages, and common type errors in plugins
Use Docker to build a container image of a Backstage project: yarn build:backend, the Dockerfile the CLI generates, host versus multi-stage builds and runtime configuration

sources.cite: CNCF, Certified Backstage Associate (CBA) certification page
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the certification body's page, found by WebSearch. Confirms the exam domains and weights: Backstage Development Workflow 24%, Backstage Infrastructure 22%, Backstage Catalog 22%, Customizing Backstage 32%. The objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: yarn backstage-cli versions:bump bumps all @backstage packages to the latest release on the main line (monthly), and bumping them together maintains the dependencies between them.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a plugin's external routes (createExternalRouteRef) are bound once at app startup with bindRoutes in createApp, in the app's App.tsx.

Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the page found by search. The default scaffold uses an in-memory SQLite database, so catalog data is lost on restart (use database.client pg outside development); unpinned plugins break after a core upgrade (check versions, upgrade on a cadence); secrets belong in environment variable substitution from Kubernetes Secrets or a secrets manager, never committed in app-config.

The company, the repositories, the services and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You maintain the internal developer portal at Tallowmere, a fictional insurer. A teammate upgraded one community plugin to its newest version on Friday; since then yarn tsc fails in CI and the portal cannot be released. A security fix in the backend must ship today.
handover: The repo is a Yarn workspaces monorepo: packages/app, packages/backend and plugins/.
The plugin's newest version depends on @backstage packages one release newer than the rest of the app.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

alignPrompt.title: Two @backstage releases installed
alignPrompt.context: The app is on one Backstage release and the upgraded plugin on the next. The security fix must ship today.

choices.label: Run yarn backstage-cli versions:bump to move every @backstage package to the same release, then yarn install and yarn tsc

effects.log: Every @backstage package is on one release; the lockfile changes together.

choices.feedback: versions:bump moves all @backstage packages together, which is what keeps their APIs and types compatible.

choices.label: Pin the plugin back to its previous version for today and plan the full upgrade for next sprint

effects.log: The plugin goes back to its old version.

choices.feedback: That is safe for today's fix, but the upgrade still has to be done as a whole release later.

choices.label: Delete yarn.lock and run yarn install so everything resolves to the newest versions

effects.log: The lockfile is regenerated from scratch.

choices.feedback: Deleting the lockfile upgrades every transitive dependency at once, untested, on the day a security fix must ship.

typesPrompt.title: The plugin's route binding
typesPrompt.context: After alignment, one error remains: the plugin now requires a routeRef binding in App.tsx.

choices.label: Bind the plugin's external route in App.tsx as its upgrade notes describe, and run yarn tsc until it is clean

effects.log: The route is bound; yarn tsc passes.

choices.feedback: The type error was a real API change; fixing it is what keeps the page from failing at runtime.

choices.label: Add // @ts-expect-error on the line and open a ticket

effects.log: The error is suppressed; a ticket is open.

choices.feedback: It is visible and tracked, but the claims page will fail when someone clicks the link.

choices.label: Remove yarn tsc from CI so the build goes green
choices.feedback: Without the type check, the next mismatch reaches production unseen.

imagePrompt.title: Building the image for the fix
imagePrompt.context: The release needs a new backend image. The CLI's generated Dockerfile expects yarn build:backend first; production settings live in app-config.production.yaml with secrets from environment variables.

choices.label: Build with yarn build:backend and the multi-stage Dockerfile from a clean checkout; supply secrets as environment variables at runtime

effects.log: A clean multi-stage image is built; no secret is inside it.

choices.feedback: A clean, multi-stage build is reproducible, and runtime configuration keeps secrets out of the image.

choices.label: Use the host build: run yarn build:backend on your laptop and copy the output into the image

effects.log: The image is built from your laptop's output.

choices.feedback: The host build is supported, but your laptop's state is now part of the release.

choices.label: Copy app-config.local.yaml, with its tokens, into the image so it runs without setup

effects.log: The local config, tokens included, goes into the image.

choices.feedback: Anyone who can pull the image can read the GitHub and database tokens.

parts.modelAnswer: One plugin brought in the next Backstage release, so two versions of core packages were installed. versions:bump aligned them; the last error was a real API change, fixed in App.tsx.

alignHarm.headline: The lockfile is the build
alignHarm.body: Keep @backstage packages on one release with versions:bump; never regenerate the lockfile to fix a version mismatch.

typesHarm.headline: A type error is a runtime error waiting
typesHarm.body: Keep yarn tsc in CI and fix the API change the error points to.

imageHarm.headline: Configuration at runtime
imageHarm.body: Secrets come from environment variables at runtime, never from a config file inside the image.

scoring.modelReasoning: Backstage's @backstage packages move together on a release train; mixing releases installs duplicate core packages and breaks types, so align them with backstage-cli versions:bump rather than pinning one plugin forward or regenerating the lockfile. A remaining type error after alignment is usually a real API change: fix it and keep yarn tsc in CI. Build the backend with build:backend and the generated multi-stage Dockerfile from a clean checkout, and supply configuration and secrets at runtime.
